Indian Ocean currents - seasonal monsoon reversal, WICC

accepted.s: Which one of the following ocean currents is correctly classified as a cold current of the Indian Ocean?
accepted.x: The West Australian Current is a cold current of the Indian Ocean. Agulhas and Mozambique are warm Indian Ocean currents, while Brazil is a warm South Atlantic current.
accepted.tq: Use current type and ocean together to eliminate reversed classifications.
accepted.sec: Ocean currents - warm or cold, and ocean (odd-one-out)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Humboldt — Cold current of the South Pacific
2. Falkland — Cold current of the South Atlantic
3. Kuroshio — Cold current of the North Pacific
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Humboldt and Falkland are correctly matched with their oceans and cold classification. Kuroshio is a warm current of the North Pacific, not a cold current.
accepted.tq: Check both the current type and the ocean before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Ocean currents - warm or cold, and ocean (odd-one-out)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Benguela Current is a cold South Atlantic current flowing along south-western Africa, particularly Namibia. California is in the North Pacific, Labrador in the North Atlantic, and Canary in the North Atlantic.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure current–ocean pair and reject options with a shifted ocean or coast.
accepted.sec: Ocean currents - warm or cold, and ocean (odd-one-out)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to ocean currents, consider the following statements:
1. Warm currents generally flow from the equator towards the poles.
2. Cold currents generally carry polar water towards the equator.
3. Warm currents usually occur along the western coasts of continents in low and middle latitudes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Warm currents generally move poleward from the equator, while cold currents carry polar water equatorward. In low and middle latitudes, warm currents usually flow along the eastern coasts of continents, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversed east-coast/west-coast comparison in a geography statement.
accepted.sec: Ocean currents - warm or cold, and ocean (odd-one-out)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct classification of the Agulhas, Brazil and Humboldt currents respectively?
accepted.x: The Agulhas and Brazil currents are warm currents, whereas the Humboldt or Peruvian Current is a cold current.
accepted.tq: Separate the two warm-current examples from the South Pacific cold-current exception.
accepted.sec: Ocean currents - warm or cold, and ocean (odd-one-out)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Norwegian Current — Warm current of the North Atlantic
Florida Current — Warm current of the North Atlantic
Labrador Current — Warm current off north-western Africa
Gulf Stream — Warm current of the North Atlantic
accepted.x: The Labrador Current is a cold current off the coast of Canada in the North Atlantic. The Canary Current, not the Labrador Current, flows off north-western Africa and is also cold.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong coast and type combination rather than relying on the current name alone.
accepted.sec: Ocean currents - warm or cold, and ocean (odd-one-out)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is an odd one out on the basis of its current type?
accepted.x: Oyashio is a cold current of the North Pacific. Agulhas, Mozambique and Kuroshio are warm currents.
accepted.tq: Identify the only current whose type differs from the other three.
accepted.sec: Ocean currents - warm or cold, and ocean (odd-one-out)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding ocean currents:
1. Solar heating contributes to the movement of ocean currents.
2. Wind and gravity influence ocean currents.
3. The Coriolis force deflects moving water to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere.
4. Density differences have no role in the movement of ocean currents.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Solar heating, wind, gravity, the Coriolis force and density differences all influence ocean currents. Therefore, statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute negative statement when the process has several recognised causes.
accepted.sec: Ocean currents - warm or cold, and ocean (odd-one-out)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): Cold, salty ocean water tends to sink.
Reason (R): An increase in salinity increases the density of ocean water.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true, and the greater density of cold, salty water explains why it tends to sink.
accepted.tq: Check whether the reason directly explains the physical process stated in the assertion.
accepted.sec: Ocean currents - warm or cold, and ocean (odd-one-out)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Current)
 a. Mozambique
 b. Falkland
 c. Oyashio
 d. California

List-II (Classification)
 i. Cold current of the North Pacific
 ii. Warm current of the Indian Ocean
 iii. Cold current of the South Atlantic
 iv. Cold current of the North Pacific

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Mozambique is a warm Indian Ocean current; Falkland is a cold South Atlantic current; Oyashio and California are cold North Pacific currents.
accepted.tq: Begin with the distinctive Mozambique–Indian Ocean pair and complete the remaining matches.
accepted.sec: Ocean currents - warm or cold, and ocean (odd-one-out)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs consists entirely of cold currents?
accepted.x: Humboldt is a cold South Pacific current and Benguela is a cold South Atlantic current. The other pairs contain warm currents only or entirely warm currents.
accepted.tq: Classify both members of each pair before choosing the all-cold combination.
accepted.sec: Ocean currents - warm or cold, and ocean (odd-one-out)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The current flowing off Japan in the North Pacific and the current flowing off Brazil in the South Atlantic are respectively:
accepted.x: Kuroshio is the warm North Pacific current off Japan, while Brazil is the warm South Atlantic current off Brazil.
accepted.tq: Use the coastal location as the primary clue and then verify the ocean basin.
accepted.sec: Ocean currents - warm or cold, and ocean (odd-one-out)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Indian Ocean circulation is correct?
o: The South Indian Ocean has a permanent clockwise gyre.
The North Indian Ocean currents reverse direction seasonally with the monsoon winds.
The North Indian Ocean has permanent gyres that do not respond to monsoon winds.
Both the North and South Indian Ocean currents reverse direction every six months.
accepted.x: The North Indian Ocean is unique among the major oceans in having currents that reverse seasonally with the monsoon winds. The South Indian Ocean has a permanent anticlockwise gyre.
accepted.tq: Use the unique seasonal-reversal feature to distinguish the North Indian Ocean from steady oceanic gyres.
accepted.sec: Indian Ocean currents - seasonal monsoon reversal, WICC  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following components of the South Indian Ocean anticlockwise gyre in the order in which they are listed from the southern and eastern African side around the gyre towards Australia:
A. Agulhas Current
B. West Wind Drift
C. West Australian Current
D. South Equatorial Current
accepted.x: The listed sequence is South Equatorial Current, Agulhas Current, West Wind Drift and West Australian Current, representing the normal anticlockwise circulation of the South Indian Ocean.
accepted.tq: Follow the circulation path continuously instead of matching isolated current names.
accepted.sec: Indian Ocean currents - seasonal monsoon reversal, WICC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: During the southwest monsoon, which one of the following combinations is correct?
o: Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal circulation is anticlockwise; WICC flows southward; EICC flows northward
Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal circulation is anticlockwise; WICC flows northward; EICC flows southward
Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal circulation is clockwise; WICC flows southward; EICC flows northward
Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal circulation is clockwise; WICC flows northward; EICC flows southward
accepted.x: During the southwest monsoon, the circulation in the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal is clockwise. The West India Coastal Current flows southward, while the East India Coastal Current flows northward.
accepted.tq: Read all three seasonal directions together; one reversed component makes a combination false.
accepted.sec: Indian Ocean currents - seasonal monsoon reversal, WICC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: During the northeast monsoon, the North Indian Ocean circulation and the direction of the northeast monsoon current are respectively:
accepted.x: In winter, during the northeast monsoon, North Indian Ocean circulation becomes anticlockwise and the northeast monsoon current flows westward.
accepted.tq: Pair the season with both the gyre direction and current direction to avoid a single-feature guess.
accepted.sec: Indian Ocean currents - seasonal monsoon reversal, WICC  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the West India Coastal Current (WICC):
1. It flows northward from November to February.
2. It flows southward during the southwest monsoon.
3. Its northward flow is described as poleward.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The WICC flows northward, or poleward, during November–February and turns southward during the southwest monsoon. All three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Combine the seasonal dates, direction and geographic description before selecting the code.
accepted.sec: Indian Ocean currents - seasonal monsoon reversal, WICC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the East India Coastal Current?
o: It flows northward throughout the year without seasonal reversal.
It flows southward throughout the year under the influence of the southwest monsoon.
It flows southward during February–September and northward during October–December.
It flows northward during February–September and southward during October–December.
accepted.x: The East India Coastal Current flows northward from February to September, with its strongest flow before the monsoon, and southward from October to December.
accepted.tq: Use the paired seasonal months to distinguish EICC from the oppositely changing WICC.
accepted.sec: Indian Ocean currents - seasonal monsoon reversal, WICC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Findlater Current is associated with which one of the following?
o: The Labrador Current and the Gulf Stream in the North Atlantic
The Somali Jet and the Arabian Sea
The Kuroshio Current and the North Pacific
The West Australian Current and the South Indian Ocean gyre
accepted.x: The Findlater Current is an Arabian Sea current associated with the Somali Jet and reverses direction with the monsoon winds.
accepted.tq: Link the named current to its associated jet and ocean region.
accepted.sec: Indian Ocean currents - seasonal monsoon reversal, WICC  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): The Findlater Current produces coastal upwelling off the Horn of Africa during the southwest monsoon.
Reason (R): The current is connected with the Somali Jet and reverses with the monsoon winds.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true. However, the association and seasonal reversal of the Findlater Current describe its behaviour; they do not by themselves constitute the direct explanation that coastal winds produce upwelling off the Horn of Africa.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a true associated fact from a reason that directly explains the asserted process.
accepted.sec: Indian Ocean currents - seasonal monsoon reversal, WICC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about upwelling associated with the Findlater Current is correct?
o: It occurs off Australia during the northeast monsoon and prevents fishing.
It occurs only in the Bay of Bengal during the southwest monsoon and controls the Indian monsoon.
It occurs off the Horn of Africa during the southwest monsoon and supports good fishing.
It occurs in the North Atlantic during winter and strengthens the Gulf Stream.
accepted.x: During the southwest monsoon, the Findlater Current creates coastal upwelling off the Horn of Africa, producing favourable fishing conditions.
accepted.tq: Apply the current–season–location relationship to the coastal upwelling scenario.
accepted.sec: Indian Ocean currents - seasonal monsoon reversal, WICC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Why is the influence of the Findlater Current on the Indian monsoon considered limited?
o: It is unrelated to the Somali Jet and monsoon winds.
It flows only in the South Atlantic Ocean.
Its upwelling zone is small, unlike the broader influence associated with the Indian Ocean Dipole.
It is a cold current that never reverses direction.
accepted.x: The upwelling zone produced by the Findlater Current is small, so its influence on the Indian monsoon is limited compared with the Indian Ocean Dipole.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated limiting factor rather than confusing it with the current’s direction or location.
accepted.sec: Indian Ocean currents - seasonal monsoon reversal, WICC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the Indian Ocean with the Atlantic and Pacific oceans regarding surface-current behaviour?
o: All three ocean systems have identical seasonal current reversals.
North Indian Ocean currents reverse seasonally, whereas Atlantic and Pacific gyres are generally steady.
Pacific currents reverse only during winter, whereas Indian Ocean currents never reverse.
Atlantic currents reverse seasonally, whereas North Indian Ocean currents are permanent.
accepted.x: North Indian Ocean currents reverse with the monsoon winds, unlike the generally steady gyres of the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
accepted.tq: Focus on the contrast between seasonal reversal and permanent or steady gyre circulation.
accepted.sec: Indian Ocean currents - seasonal monsoon reversal, WICC  [APPSC]
